value.name: Kenneth questions dual-time watch
value.description: Kenneth notices Miles's two-time-zone watch and questions why he would need it in Beverly Hills.
evidence: KENNETH Why would you need two time zones? You never leave Beverly Hills.
MILES It was a gift from a client.

value.name: Miles explains watch gift
value.description: Miles says the dual-time-zone watch was given to him by a client.
evidence: MILES It was a gift from a client.

value.name: Kenneth mocks Beverly Hills lifestyle
value.description: Kenneth sarcastically suggests setting one side of the watch for Bel Air, underscoring their shallow local routine.
evidence: KENNETH Set one side for Bel Air.

value.name: Miles laments lost aspirations
value.description: Miles reacts bitterly to the conversation and says they once had ambitions in college.
evidence: MILES Botox. Christ. We had aspirations when we were in college.

value.name: Kenneth denies shared ambition
value.description: Kenneth rejects Miles's nostalgia and insists they did not actually have the ambitions Miles remembers.

value.name: Miles recalls career ambitions
value.description: Miles names the lofty careers he once imagined for himself and Kenneth, contrasting them with their current lives.
evidence: MILES You were going to be a Cardiac Surgeon. I was going to clerk for the Supreme Court.

value.name: Kenneth reveals cynical life plans
value.description: Kenneth undercuts the idealized past by claiming he only planned to play golf and that Miles was expected to have Asian girlfriends.
evidence: KENNETH I was going to play golf. You were going to have Asian girlfriends.

value.name: Miles jokes about denial
value.description: Miles responds with a cynical joke, signaling his frustration and self-awareness.
evidence: MILES Denial is not a river in Egypt.

value.name: Kenneth puts Miles in check
value.description: Kenneth moves a chess piece and declares that Miles is in check, shifting the scene from banter to the game state.

value.name: Miles admits need for therapy
value.description: Miles responds to being in check by saying he should be in therapy, revealing emotional dissatisfaction.
evidence: MILES I should be in therapy.
